newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby banker fined over campaign gifts - report.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby banker fined over campaign gifts - report.

text.p: California investment banker Calvin Grigsby, whose firm underwrites municipal bonds, was fined for improperly providing a campaign contribution to a mayoral candidate, according to a published report.
Grigsby was not immediately available to comment on the report.
The San Francisco Examiner newspaper reported Friday evening that Grigsby was fined $5,000 over the contribution and for failing to file required disclosure statements.

The state's Fair Political Practices Commission found that Grigsby loaned $5,000 to an attorney in 1993 with the understanding that she would donate it to Alameda County Supervisor Mary King, who was then running for mayor of Oakland, Calif., the Examiner reported.

Grigsby also was found to have violated the state's Fair Political Practices Act by failing to file required disclosure statements for the $53,500 he and Fiscal Funding, a firm he controls, gave to candidates in 1993, the newspaper said.

Grigsby's firm, Grigsby Brandford & Co of San Francisco, has underwritten more than $1 billion worth of bonds for Alameda County. His firm is one of the largest African American owned municipal bond underwriters in the U.S.
Grigsby has already paid the fine, the Examiner reported.
